entities.summary:
Titus Cloelius Siculus was a Roman statesman of the early Republic, who served as one of the first consular tribunes in 444 BC.




He was compelled to abdicate after a fault was found during his election, two years later he was one of the founders of the colony of Ardea.




This event marked a significant turning point in the early Republic, as it highlighted the need for greater accountability and transparency in government.





This event also had a lasting impact on the development of Roman governance, with the introduction of consular tribunes as a means of balancing power between the consuls and the common people.





The legacy of Titus Cloelius Siculus can be seen in the continued development of the Roman Republic, with his ideas on governance and accountability influencing later Roman leaders.





In conclusion, Titus Cloelius Siculus was a pivotal figure in the early Republic, whose actions had far-reaching consequences for the development of Roman governance and the shaping of the Roman Republic.
